line_or_section: score_predictions_v4.py V21 block (S['V21'] = ("miss", ...)); scores row V21
finding: V21 is still hard coded (now 'miss' instead of hit); the computed frame lr is still unused, so the A03 fix did not make the verdict follow the data. The evidence text is false: it says the SiK radio is 'the slowest link where it completes', but LoRaWAN DR5 with the hybrid session (arch B) completes with recovery of 734 s (drone) and 735 s (robot). By the registered clause (prediction above 1 s, refuted below 1 s) on the slowest robotics link, the verdict is hit, or not scored if DR0 is taken as the slowest link. It is not a miss. The scorer also reads the drone row, although the question names a robotics link (robot SiK B is 0.956 s).
evidence: mission/results/base.csv: ttra_s_median drone B lora_dr5 734.35, robot B lora_dr5 735.44, drone B sik 0.912, robot B sik 0.956; B lora_dr0 NaN. MISSION_STUDY.md lines 88 and 111 show 734.35 and 735.44. PROTOCOL_SIM.md line 49: mavlink2_pq hybrid on DR0 9.9 h; line 88: SiK hybrid 1.36 s (above 1 s even on SiK).
suggested_fix: Compute V21 from base.csv: take the slowest link (by rate) on which arch B completes for the robot vehicle (LoRaWAN DR5, 735 s), then score hit; or mark it not scored with the reason that DR0 never completes in the mission run. Remove the hard coded string, regenerate the scores, and log the change in RUN_LOG.

finding: V11 is hard coded 'between', which does not follow the verdict rules printed in the same file ('between when neither holds'). The prediction holds literally: the largest error of the formula is 0.42 percent, at most 1 percent. The concern is that three of the four examples are not independent tests, which is a reason for 'not scored' or 'hit, weak', not for 'between'. The filter on the model name OR abs error below 10 still silently drops the -64.1 percent row, so the computed worst_l is selective (A05).

suggested_fix: Score V11 by its clause from the formula rows (hit) and add the weakness note, or mark it not scored with the reason. Either way, compute the verdict instead of writing the string, and state in the evidence text that the third round model row is excluded and why.

line_or_section: section 4.4 closed form table rows 'duty cycle wait, 11 B / 51 B at DR0'; status row 'duty cycle'; validate_v4.py closed_form_rows
finding: The duty cycle 'closed form check' runs on linksim/model.py Link.air_s (8 x bytes / 250 bit/s, no PHY or LoRaWAN overhead). The same section calls this the third round air time and shows it is 64 percent too fast. The check compares Link.off_s(air) with 99 x air, the same formula as off_s, so it cannot fail. The protocol and mission simulations use lora.time_on_air_s, whose duty cycle path is not checked. The V13 hit rests partly on this check.
evidence: 34.848 / 99 = 0.352 s = 11 x 8 / 250, and 161.568 / 99 = 1.632 s = 51 x 8 / 250. model.py lines 60 to 67: air_s = 8*wire/rate and off_s = air*(1/duty - 1). validate_v4.py: L = model.build_links(p)['lorawan'].
suggested_fix: Run the duty cycle check through the LoRa link class of linksim/lora.py that PROTOCOL_SIM uses, at DR0 with the 13 B LoRaWAN overhead. Describe it as an arithmetic check of one line, not a validation, and note this beside V13.

line_or_section: V8 evidence ('every other part below 1 mJ'); PAPER line 64 ('likely low by about that factor')
finding: The V8 evidence states as fact that every part except ESP32-C3 is below 1 mJ. That holds only for the uncalibrated estimate, which the paper says is low by a median of 54.8 percent, a factor of about 2.2. With that factor the LDO operating points of STM32L4R5, STM32L552 and STM32L476 also exceed 1 mJ. The paper's phrase 'low by about that factor' uses a percent as a factor and leaves the size unclear. The verdict (miss) does not change.
evidence: energy_per_op.csv mldsa44_verify: STM32L4R5 LDO 516 uJ, STM32L552 LDO 497 uJ, STM32L476 LDO 469 uJ; 1/(1-0.548) = 2.21, so about 1140, 1100 and 1040 uJ calibrated.
suggested_fix: In V8 and in PAPER section 4.2, state the factor (about 2.2) and that three more parts would exceed 1 mJ after calibration. Alternatively, report V8 on both the uncalibrated and the calibrated estimate.
